full_volume_followup.reason: The generation rotated the ground axes into an isometric view, contradicting the screen-aligned floor plan.
full_volume_followup.prompt:
Create a native-transparent modular dungeon WALL VOLUME atlas, using the supplied image ONLY as the canonical stone material/color reference. This is a new geometrically consistent sprite kit, not a recolor of its old shapes.

CRITICAL FIXED CAMERA:
Orthographic three-quarter projection, identical everywhere. Ground X is screen-right; ground Y is screen-down. Every elevation edge projects from TOP to FOOT by vector (+16,+96) at reference scale, meaning DOWN and slightly RIGHT. There is exactly ONE camera; no mirrored camera for a west or east wall. The visible lateral wall face is on the RIGHT of a vertical wall, regardless of where the wall will be used. All vertical elevation edges slope the SAME direction, down-right at ratio 1:6. Lighting comes from image upper left for the entire atlas.

A wall must be an actual tall masonry VOLUME: cap TOP plane, a small dark cap front lip, TWO continuous brick courses under it, and the foot at floor level. For a horizontal wall the cap and complete front facade share the SAME elevation vector and their surfaces are physically joined with no dark empty gap. For a vertical wall, its right side face is a narrow parallelogram: top end at top-plane corner, foot displaced (+16,+96); same at its lower end. No front closing face on open connection ports. All surfaces share one height; do not make vertical pieces little flat dominoes or cubes on the floor. Ground is not drawn. A side-plane edge that joins another module is an open masonry port, not a chamfer. Corners have square L top footprints and continue the correct side/front planes, never a giant black wedge.

LAYOUT:
1536x1536 RGBA, a 3 columns by 3 rows atlas, each slot512x512, at least40px transparent gutters. Nine separate COMPLETE reusable sprites, no labels:
row1 col1: horizontal wall section, three cap stones across, top footprint about360px wide x64px deep, full 96px masonry height below its front edge.
row1 col2: vertical wall section, three cap stones end-to-end along screen Y, top footprint about64px wide x300px long, right-side masonry plane projects (+16,+96); both ends are OPEN connection ports, no stair feet on individual top stones.
row1 col3: shorter vertical wall section, two cap stones, top footprint64x200, exactly same right-side projection and stone material.
row2 col1: OUTER NW L corner, arms extend RIGHT and DOWN from its corner; both native arms about160px, top thickness64, full masonry volume below, same fixed (+16,+96) projection.
row2 col2: OUTER NE L corner, arms extend LEFT and DOWN; full volume, SAME camera, no mirrored projection.
row2 col3: OUTER SW L corner, arms extend RIGHT and UP; full volume, SAME camera.
row3 col1: OUTER SE L corner, arms extend LEFT and UP; full volume, SAME camera.
row3 col2: INNER (concave) corner joining a horizontal wall with a vertical wall, arms extend RIGHT and UP, negative-space notch visible; full consistent masonry volume.
row3 col3: INNER concave counterpart, arms extend LEFT and UP, same camera.

All TOP planes share the reference image's horizontal cap material: subdued blue slate, typical center sRGB(72,92,128), modest facets(80,100,135), restrained edge highlights(130,147,177). Faces in shadow around(38,49,68). Small cracks and subtle chips, quiet painted texture, thick black outer silhouettes in the same proportional stroke throughout. No bright blue verticals versus gray corners. Brick courses are offset and touching by narrow masonry joints. No transparent gaps between the cap and its own wall, nor between stones in each module. Genuine transparent background, no drop-shadow haze, floor tiles, objects, torches, ground or full-room illustration. This is a modular engineering art sheet with one strictly enforced camera and material.
